title: feat/core: Implement Command Line Interface (CLI)
body: # Description This PR implements the Command Line Interface (CLI) for the Job Worker Service. It provides a robust, user-friendly terminal interface to interact with the gRPC server, enabling users to start, stop, monitor, and stream logs from isolated Linux processes. The CLI is built using `cobra` and enforces strict mTLS authentication for all communications. It supports flexible configuration via command-line flags or environment variables and includes features for scripting (JSON output, quiet mode) and interactivity (log streaming). ## Testing Strategy The CLI implementation is verified through a combination of unit tests with mocks and manual integration testing: 1. **Unit Tests (`internal/cli/*_test.go`)**: * **Command Logic**: The core logic for `start`, `stop`, `status`, and `stream` is tested using a `mockJobWorkerClient`. This verifies that flags are correctly parsed and passed to the gRPC client, and that responses are formatted correctly (Text vs. JSON). * **Wiring**: Tests ensure that the Cobra root command correctly wires up flags and subcommands. * **Authentication**: `auth_test.go` verifies that TLS configurations are loaded correctly from disk and handles error scenarios (missing files, invalid certs). * **Utilities**: Helper functions for environment variables and JSON printing are covered. 2. **Integration Verification**: * Verified end-to-end connectivity with the running `worker-server`. * Confirmed mTLS handshake success with valid certificates and rejection with invalid ones. * Verified raw binary output streaming works as expected without corruption. ## Type of change - [ ] Scaffolding (initial setup) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] Refactor (code improvement without functionality change) - [ ] Documentation update # Changelog - **CLI Structure**: Implemented `worker-cli` entry point using `spf13/cobra`. - **Commands**: Added `start`, `stop`, `status`, `stream`, and `version` commands. - **Security**: Implemented mTLS connection logic, loading CA, client cert, and key from configurable paths. - **UX Improvements**: - Added `--json` flag for machine-readable output. - Added `--quiet` (`-q`) flag for scripting (printing only IDs). - Added `--follow` (`-f`) flag to `start` to immediately stream logs. - Added environment variable support (e.g., `WORKER_ADDR`) for all flags. - **Output Handling**: Implemented raw byte streaming for logs to support binary output without encoding issues. # Challenge Requirements - [x] **Concurrency**: The CLI handles streaming responses efficiently. - [x] **Error Handling**: Runtime errors are reported clearly without printing help usage (`SilenceUsage: true`). Context cancellation (Ctrl+C) is handled gracefully. - [x] **Security**: mTLS is mandatory. No secrets are hardcoded; credentials are loaded from files. - [x] **Dependencies**: Uses standard `cobra` and `grpc` libraries. # Checklist: - [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project - [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code - [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas - [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation - [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works - [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes # Screenshots: ## Start Job ## Status (Running) ## Stop ## Stream ## Status (Stopped)

title: feat/core: Implement gRPC Server with Authentication
body: # Description This PR implements the core gRPC server for the Job Worker service, enforcing strict mTLS authentication and identity-based authorization. It also finalizes the log streaming architecture by refactoring the `OutputBuffer` to use a robust, pull-based iterator pattern (`LogStream`) instead of channels. This ensures correct error propagation and efficient resource usage during concurrent streaming. ## Type of change - [ ] Scaffolding (initial setup) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - title: feat/core: Implement Worker Library (Stream/Status)
body: # Implement Job Streaming & Status Reporting ## Summary This PR extends the `worker` library to support real-time output streaming and thread-safe status querying. It introduces a concurrent `OutputBuffer` to handle log broadcasting with history replay and updates the `Job` struct to expose its lifecycle state via a dedicated `Status()` method. ## Key Changes ### 1. Output Streaming (`internal/worker`) * **OutputBuffer**: Implemented a thread-safe buffer (`internal/worker/output_buffer.go`) that captures `stdout` and `stderr` from the process. * Uses `sync.Cond` to broadcast logs to multiple concurrent listeners efficiently. * Supports **History Replay**: Clients connecting late receive the full log history from the start of execution. * **Source Tagging**: Distinguishes between `stdout` and `stderr` in the log stream. * **Job Integration**: * Wired `exec.Cmd` output streams to the `OutputBuffer` in `createCommand`. * Added `Job.Stream(ctx)` to expose the log iterator to consumers. * Ensured streams are closed correctly during `waitAndCleanup` and `abortStart`. ### 2. Status Reporting * **Job.Status()**: Added a method to return a thread-safe snapshot of the `Lifecycle` struct (Status, ExitCode, StartTime, EndTime). * **Refactoring**: Moved `LogEntry` and `OutputSource` definitions to `types.go` to centralize domain types. ## Testing Summary #### 1. Output Streaming (Integration & Unit) * **Real-time Capture**: Verifies that a shell script writing to both stdout and stderr is correctly captured and streamed to a client. * **Concurrency**: Confirms that multiple clients can read the same stream without race conditions. * **History Replay**: Confirms that late subscribers receive all previous logs. * **Source Tagging**: Verifies correct tagging of stdout vs stderr. * **Edge Cases**: Covers writing to closed buffers and context cancellation. #### 2. Lifecycle & Status Tests * **Status Verification**: Updated existing integration tests to use `Job.Status()` for assertions. * **Timestamp Checks**: Added assertions to ensure `StartTime` and `EndTime` are correctly populated during state transitions. * **Exit Code Accuracy**: Verified that `ExitCode` is initialized to `-1` and correctly updated upon completion or failure. ## Pre-Submission Checklist - [x] **Formatting**: Ran `go fmt ./...` - [x] **Static Analysis**: Ran `go vet ./...` - [x] **Race Detection**: Ran `go test -race ./...` - [x] **Dependencies**: Ran `go mod tidy` - [x] **Code Generation**: Ran `make proto` ## Screenshots ### Testing Coverage for Worker (Root vs User)

title: feat/core: Implement Worker Library (Start/Stop)
body: # Implement Core Worker Library (Start/Stop) ## Summary This PR implements the core `worker` library for managing Linux processes with Cgroup resource isolation. It establishes the foundational architecture for the job worker service, including process orchestration, lifecycle management, and comprehensive integration testing. Note: The gRPC server and CLI will be implemented in subsequent PRs. ## Key Changes ### 1. Worker Library (`internal/worker`) * **Job Lifecycle**: Implemented the `Job` struct to manage the full lifecycle of a Linux process, including `Start`, `Stop`, and asynchronous cleanup (`waitAndCleanup`). * **Cgroup Isolation**: Implemented a `Cgroup` controller (v2) to enforce CPU, Memory, and I/O limits. * Includes logic to create, attach, and delete cgroups. * Added `Kill()` support using `cgroup.kill` (Linux 5.14+) for reliable process tree termination. * **Process Orchestration**: Implemented `ptrace`-based orchestration to ensure child processes are paused and attached to the correct cgroup *before* execution begins. ### 2. Testing & Tooling * **Integration Tests** and **Unit Tests**: Added comprehensive integration tests covering: * **Makefile**: Added targets for building, testing (`test`, `test-race`), and generating coverage reports (`test-cover-html`). ### Testing Summary #### 1. Job Lifecycle (Integration) * **Happy Path**: Verifies that a standard job starts, transitions to running, executes successfully, and completes with exit code 0. * **Manual Stop**: Confirms that stopping a job immediately transitions it to the stopped state and triggers asynchronous resource cleanup. * **Context Cancellation**: Verifies that canceling the context passed to the start method kills the underlying process and cleans up resources. * **Exit Codes**: Ensures that processes exiting with non-zero codes are correctly marked as failed and the specific exit code is captured. * **Short-Lived Processes**: Validates that the orchestration logic handles race conditions correctly for processes that exit immediately. #### 2. Resource Isolation & Enforcement (Root Integration) * **Memory Limits**: Compiles a helper binary to verify that the Linux kernel OOM killer terminates a process attempting to allocate memory beyond the configured Cgroup limit. * **Process Tree Cleanup**: Spawns a shell script creating background child processes to verify that stopping a job successfully terminates the entire process tree, preventing orphaned processes. #### 3. Unit Tests * **Cgroup File Generation**: Validates that resource limits (Memory, CPU, I/O) are correctly formatted and written to the Cgroup controller files. * **PID Attachment**: Verifies the logic for writing PIDs to the Cgroup processes file. * **Job Initialization**: Checks default state values, ID generation, and input validation for working directories. * **State Guards**: Ensures invalid state transitions (e.g., starting an already running job) are prevented. #### 4. Error Handling * **Invalid Commands**: Verifies that attempting to run a non-existent binary results in a failed status. * **Infrastructure Failures**: Verifies that the job fails gracefully if the Cgroup directory cannot be created. * **Partial Write Failures**: Ensures that if applying Cgroup limits fails halfway through (e.g., permission denied), the directory is cleaned up to prevent leaks. ## Pre-Submission Checklist - [x] **Formatting**: Ran `go fmt ./...` - [x] **Static Analysis**: Ran `go vet ./...` - [x] **Race Detection**: Ran `go test -race ./...` - [x] **Dependencies**: Ran `go mod tidy` - [x] **Code Generation**: Ran `make proto` ## Screenshots ### Testing Coverage for Worker (Root vs User)

title: docs/rfd: Design for Prototype Job Worker Service
body:
# PR Description: Design for Prototype Job Worker Service

## Summary
This PR introduces the design specification (RFD) for a prototype Job Worker Service. The service provides a gRPC API to manage the lifecycle of arbitrary processes on **Linux** environments.

### Diagrams
#### Architecture
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Client"
        C1[CLI A]
        C2[CLI B]
    end

    subgraph "Worker Service (Host)"
        SVR[gRPC Server]
        MAP[(Jobs Map)]
        
        subgraph "Memory Store"
            B1[OutputBuffer: Job 1]
            B2[OutputBuffer: Job 2]
        end

        subgraph "Kernel Control Groups"
            subgraph "Cgroup: job-1"
                P1((Shell Process))
                P1_C1((Child: Sleep))
            end
            
            subgraph "Cgroup: job-2"
                P2((Binary Process))
            end

            CG[[Cgroups v2: io, cpu, mem]]
        end
    end

    %% Networking & Auth
    C1 -- "Job 1" --> SVR
    C2 -- "Job 2" --> SVR
    SVR <--> MAP

    %% Mapping to Buffers
    MAP --> B1
    MAP --> B2
    
    %% Execution & Resource Binding
    SVR -- "os/exec" --> P1
    SVR -- "os/exec" --> P2
    P1 & P1_C1 & P2 --- CG

    %% Output Flow
    P1 -.-> B1 -.-> SVR
    P2 -.-> B2 -.-> SVR
    SVR -- "gRPC Stream" --> C1
```

#### Sequence Diagram of golden flow
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as CLI
    participant S as gRPC Server
    participant L as Library
    participant K as Linux Kernel (Cgroups)
    participant P as Process Tree

    Note over C, P: StartRequest() Sequence
    C->>S: StartRequest(cmd, limits)
    S->>S: Authorize (Extract CN)
    S->>L: NewJob() & Init Cgroup
    L->>K: mkdir /sys/fs/cgroup/worker/123
    L->>K: write limits (mem, cpu, io)
    
    Note over L, P: Ptrace-Controlled Orchestration
    L->>K: fork() with Ptrace bit set
    K->>P: Create Process (Status: STOPPED)
    L->>K: write PID to cgroup.procs
    Note over K, P: Child is jailed while execution is frozen
    L->>K: PtraceDetach(PID)
    K->>P: Resume Execution (execve)
    
    L-->>S: Job ID: 123
    S-->>C: StartResponse

    Note over C, P: StreamRequest() Sequence
    C->>S: StreamRequest(123)
    S->>L: Get Stream(123)
    L-->>C: Replay existing LogEntries
    
    loop Real-time Tail (Push Model)
        P->>L: io.Writer.Write(data)
        L->>L: Append LogEntry to OutputBuffer
        L->>L: sync.Cond.Broadcast()
        L-->>C: LogChunk (Live)
    end

    Note over C, P: StopRequest() Sequence
    C->>S: StopRequest(123)
    S->>S: Authorize (CN == Owner)
    S->>L: StopJob(123)
    
    Note right of L: Atomic Tree Termination
    L->>K: Write "1" to .../123/cgroup.kill
    K->>P: SIGKILL all processes in Cgroup
    P-->>K: Processes Terminated
    
    L->>L: Update Lifecycle (Status: Stopped, EndTime: now)
    L-->>S: Success
    S-->>C: StopResponse ("Job 123 stopped")

    Note over L, K: Post-Termination Cleanup
    L->>K: rmdir /sys/fs/cgroup/worker/123
```
